items.title: The associations between job stress and physical and mental health in firefighters: a systematic review.
items.authors: Pakdel FK, Pakdel AK, Zadeh MS, Abbasi S, Polkoii OT.

sections.text: Firefighters are exposed to psychosocial stressors including interpersonal conflict, organizational injustice, and discrimination. This systematic review investigated the associations between work-related psychosocial stress and physical and mental health outcomes among firefighters. A comprehensive search was performed in PubMed, PsycINFO, CINAHL, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar from inception to May 2026. Original cross-sectional, longitudinal, and cohort studies examining associations between job stress and health outcomes in firefighters were included. The review focused on six outcome domains: (1) depression and suicidality, (2) non-depressive mental health problems (PTSD symptoms, anxiety, burnout), (3) alcohol use disorders, (4) sleep quality, (5) somatic disorders (cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, gastrointestinal), and (6) physical performance. Quality assessment was conducted using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). A thematic narrative synthesis was employed due to methodological heterogeneity. Findings were synthesized narratively, with key odds ratios (ORs) extracted and presented in summary tables. Thirty-four original studies involving 87,242 firefighters across Asia, North America, Europe, and South America were included. The strongest associations were observed for organizational system stress with self-reported depressive symptoms (OR = 8.03 in the longitudinal study), discrimination and harassment with self-reported PTSD symptoms (OR = 2.21) and anxiety (OR = 2.56) in female firefighters, and lack of reward with gastrointestinal disorders (OR = 2.17-2.39) and musculoskeletal disorders (OR = 2.39). Protective factors including social support, self-efficacy, and resilience consistently buffered stress-related health outcomes. Physical performance declined with age (12-13% decrease in strength and power), and less experienced firefighters demonstrated greater physiological stress responses. Job stress is associated with pervasive and clinically significant adverse health outcomes in firefighters. The available evidence, predominantly cross-sectional, suggests associations rather than causal effects. Organizational interventions targeting workplace fairness, conflict reduction, and anti-discrimination policies, alongside individual-level resilience training, are warranted. Protecting firefighter health through evidence-based stress prevention is an occupational health priority. CRD420261417550.

items.title: Prevalence of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder in Iranian Intensive Care Unit Survivors and Related Factors: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.authors: Salehi Tali S, Molavynejad S, Imani A, Shafiei E.

sections.text: Intensive care unit survivors are discharged with various psychological complications, among which post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is one of the most significant. The main aim of this study was to determine the prevalence of PTSD and its associated factors among Iranian intensive care unit (ICU) survivors. This systematic review and meta-analysis included studies published in English and Persian from 2000 to 2025. Electronic gateways and databases, including MEDLINE via PubMed, MEDLINE via OVID, ISI Web of Knowledge, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Library, Magiran, Wiley, Scientific Information Database (SID), and Google Scholar, were searched. Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal checklist. Data were analyzed using STATA software (version 17.0, StataCorp/LC, USA). Statistical heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic, and a random-effects model was applied to estimate pooled prevalence. A significant level of P<0.001was considered. The pooled prevalence of PTSD in Iranian ICU survivors was 36.4% (95% CI: 23.5-48.3; I2=98.75%; P<0.001). The prevalence in Iranian women, 51.47% (95% CI: 45.01-57.92; I2=97.52%), was higher than in Iranian men, 48.53% (95% CI: 42.08-54.99; I2=97.52%). Common related factors included older age, prolonged ICU hospitalization, history of psychiatric disorders, mechanical ventilation, and drug abuse. The prevalence of PTSD among Iranian ICU survivors is relatively high. Identification of associated factors underscores the need for early screening, comprehensive follow-up programs, and targeted psychological interventions, particularly for high-risk populations.

items.title: Cannabis use patterns, depression trajectories and suicide attempts: a 10-year longitudinal study.
items.authors: Maffre Maviel G, Davisse-Paturet C, Duclos A, Wiernik E, Airagnes G, Melchior M.

sections.text: Cannabis use has been consistently associated with increased risks of depression, suicidal ideation, and suicide attempt. We aimed to compare the trajectories of depression and suicide attempt risk among individuals who used cannabis before or concomitantly with the onset of depressive symptoms, relative to depressed individuals who did not use cannabis. We used data from 24,446 participants of CONSTANCES, a French national cohort, recruited between 2013-2020. People who started using cannabis before the onset of a depressive episode showed shorter durations of depression, and were half as likely to attempt suicide than the general depressed population. On the other hand, people with concomitant onset of cannabis use and depression showed similar characteristics compared to the general depressed population. These findings suggest that specific patterns of cannabis use could be linked to a lower risk of adverse mental health outcomes.

items.title: Structural vulnerability and mental health of visible minority non-health essential workers during the COVID-19 pandemic in Calgary, Canada.
items.authors: Chowdhury N, Datta R, Walsh CA, Tong H, Erman D, Rahman N, Lake D, Turin TC.

sections.text: Non-health essential workers (NHEWs), including those in food processing, grocery retail, and transportation, faced high occupational exposure during the COVID-19 pandemic with fewer protections than healthcare workers. In Canada, visible minorities are disproportionately represented in these sectors. This study aimed to assess the prevalence and determinants of stress, anxiety, and depression among VM-NHEWs in Calgary, Canada. Data were derived from a broader community-engaged survey of essential workers in Calgary. The analysis was restricted to 446 VM-NHEWs to specifically examine the experiences of this distinct workforce. Participants completed a survey including the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10), the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9), and the Generalized Anxiety Disorder scale (GAD-7). Multivariable logistic regression models were employed to identify associations between sociodemographic factors, employment conditions, and mental health outcomes. Moderate-to-high stress affected 85.6% of participants, while 37.6% and 31.1% screened positive for moderate-to-severe depression and anxiety, respectively. Female sex and employment disruption were independently associated with higher odds of depression, while living in multi-person households was strongly protective against both anxiety and depression. VM-NHEWs experienced substantial mental health burden during the pandemic, driven by intersecting structural vulnerabilities. Addressing employment precarity and delivering culturally safe mental health supports are critical for future pandemic preparedness.

items.title: Written exposure therapy as treatment for comorbid PTSD and SUD: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.authors: Fatima T, Catchlove S, Melwani S, Rowland B, Arunogiri S.

sections.text: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness, feasibility, and acceptability of Written Exposure Therapy (WET) when it is used as a component in integrated treatment of comorbid PTSD and Substance Use Disorder (SUD). A systematic review and meta-analysis was used to synthesise foundational knowledge regarding WET. Twelve studies were included and analysed in the review. Random-effects meta-analysis of six studies showed large overall pre/post decrease in PTSD severity (Hedges' g = 1.18, 95% CI [0.68, 1.72], p < 0.001). Rate of retention (69.03%) was higher than typically seen in integrated prolonged exposure treatments for PTSD-SUD. The majority of participants and providers found WET feasible and acceptable. A minority of participants found concurrent treatment for both disorders burdensome. Findings suggest that can be an effective component in integrated treatment of PTSD-SUD, owing to its efficacy, brevity, and low-burden of integration. Limitations of the current findings include small samples, lack of comparator groups, and limited information regarding treatment components and change in SUD.

items.title: The association study between dietary behaviors, lifestyle patterns and comorbid depressive and anxiety symptoms in Yunnan adolescents aged 12-19, Southwest China: a largescale cross-section screen and a propensity score matching analysis.
items.authors: Yang Y, Fang H, Chen W, Huang S, Yang X.

sections.text: The purpose of this study is to explore the association of dietary behaviors and other lifestyle habits with the presence of comorbid depressive and anxiety symptoms in adolescents aged from 12 to 19 years old in Yunnan Province in Southwest China. We conducted a complex, multi-stage stratified, probability sampling design in 57,031 participants from 253 multi-center of 129 counties of Yunnan in 2023. Participants with complete information on basic demographic information, dietary behaviors, lifestyle patterns (incuding sleep duration, screen time, and exercises etc.,), and who participated in the survey and assessed depressive and anxiety symptoms using standardized measures. Propensity score matching was performed to reduce imbalance in prespecified measured covariates between comparison groups. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to examine the association. The detection rate of total participants in the comorbid depressive and anxiety symptoms was 12.72%. And the detection rate of females in the comorbid depressive and anxiety symptoms group (15.51%) was notably higher than that of males (9.73%). After controlling for potential confounding effects through multiple logistic regression analyses, and after PSM, sedative medication misuse (OR = 4.613, 95% CI 3.734-5.699), the use of electronic devices in dark environments at night (always using: OR = 3.538, 95% CI 3.111-4.023), computer use exceeding 2 h daily (OR = 1.719, 95% CI 1.499-1.971), insufficient sleep (OR= 1.600, 95% CI 1.456-1.757), smoking (OR = 1.469, 95% CI 1.339-1.612) and alcohol consumption (OR = 1.706, 95% CI 1.572-1.851) were positive association. Consuming breakfast (OR = 0.450, 95% CI 0.380-0.532), vegetables (OR = 0.712, 95% CI 0.587-0.864), and fruits (OR = 0.705, 95% CI 0.618-0.805), the computer use < 2 h daily (OR = 0.866, 95% CI 0.801-0.936) and watching TV < 2 h (OR = 0.771, 95% CI 0.706-0.843) were negative association. Healthy dietary, sleep patterns, and digital device usage should be carefully monitored as part of adolescent mental health interventions. And longitudinal, culturally responsive, and comprehensive interventions addressing individual behaviors, family dynamics, and community-level factors are urgently needed.

items.title: Cyberbullying, Digital Victimisation and Suicidality Among Adolescents and Sexual and Gender Minority Populations: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
items.authors: Mandal D, Sutar R, Pakhre A, Singh V, Agrawal A.

sections.text: Cybersuicide refers to suicidal behaviour influenced by online activities, particularly cyberbullying and cyber-victimisation. Digital harassment is strongly linked to mental health problems that can precipitate suicidal ideation and attempts, especially among adolescents, who experience multiple forms of online abuse leading to depression, anxiety and stress. Gender minority populations may face greater risk due to minority stress and disproportionate online harassment. A comprehensive review is needed to understand this emerging public health challenge and inform targeted prevention and mental health interventions. A systematic search following PRISMA guidelines was conducted on 17 March 2025 across PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect and Cochrane CENTRAL after registering protocol on PROSPERO (CRD420251061647). Of 400 studies identified, 21 involved adolescents, youth or university students, and 7 examined gender minority populations. The pooled odds ratio for the association between cyberbullying and suicidality across 9 studies was 3.22 (95% CI: 1.9-5.5; z = 4.33, p <.0001). Pooled cyberbullying prevalence was 13.9% (95% CI: 7.8-23.5) pre-2020 and 13.2% (95% CI: 6.7-24.1) post-2020 (I² = 99.7%). Among gender minority groups, pooled prevalence was 39.89% (95% CI: 18.56-65.91). Pooled suicidal ideation prevalence was 21.39% (95% CI: 13.30-32.56). Cyberbullying is a consistent risk factor for suicidal behaviour, amplified by depression, minority stress and low social support. Strengthening digital literacy, integrating cyberbullying prevention into adolescent mental health programmes and implementing inclusive online monitoring protocols are essential to mitigate these risks.

items.title: The Plasma Proteome Mediates the Association Between Workplace Noise Exposure and Psychiatric Disorder Risk.
items.authors: Zhao X, Fu Y, Zhang DD, Xu W, Wang HF, Zhang W, Yu JT, Tan L.

sections.text: Workplace noise exposure has been linked to adverse mental health outcomes, yet the underlying biological processes remain incompletely understood. We aimed to characterize workplace noise-related plasma proteomic profiles, examine the mediating role of circulating proteins in the associations between workplace noise exposure and psychiatric disorders, and quantify individual susceptibility. Using UK Biobank data, we characterized workplace noise-related proteomic profiles and examined the associations between workplace noise exposure and incident psychiatric disorders. Proteins associated with both exposure and disease risk were identified, followed by functional enrichment and mediation analyses. Workplace Noise-related Protein Risk Scores (WNPRSs) were constructed from shared mediator proteins to assess individual susceptibility, joint risk patterns, and predictive performance. We identified 229 workplace noise-associated plasma proteins, with assay-specific enrichment predominantly involving extracellular and membrane-associated cellular components. Circulating proteins partially mediated the associations of workplace noise exposure with anxiety disorder and major depressive disorder (MDD), with mediation proportions ranging from 1.9% to 9.2% and 2.5% to 19.4%, respectively. items.title: Longitudinal Associations Between ADHD Symptoms and Cannabis Use in Adolescence: Exploration of the Dynamic Cross-Lagged Effects.
items.authors: Girard-Lapointe J, Castellanos-Ryan N, Lynch SJ, Watts JJ, Didaskalou M, Conrod PJ.
items.journal: Canadian journal of psychiatry. Revue canadienne de psychiatrie

sections.text: IntroductionAdolescence represents a period of heightened vulnerability for the initiation of psychoactive substance use, such as cannabis. A growing body of research suggests a marked co-occurrence between attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms and early or problematic cannabis use. However, most of these studies are cross-sectional, raising questions about the nature and directionality of this association. Understanding the underlying dynamics of this relationship is of particular importance for both prevention and intervention among at-risk adolescents.MethodData were drawn from CoVenture, a longitudinal study of 3,756 secondary school students from the Greater Montreal area. Each year from Grade 7 to Grade 11, participants self-reported their frequency of alcohol and cannabis use, as well as ADHD symptoms. A Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model was used to assess within-person associations over time, controlling for alcohol use and demographic covariates.ResultsAt a between-person level, cannabis use and ADHD symptoms were significantly associated, even after controlling for alcohol use. At a within-person level, findings suggest a bidirectional relationship, starting in Grade 8. Greater ADHD symptom severity significantly predicted subsequent year increases in cannabis use. The reverse pathway-from greater cannabis use to subsequent year increases in ADHD symptoms-was also significant. Further analysis showed that higher cannabis use in Grade 9 increased the risk of reaching a clinically relevant level of ADHD symptoms in Grade 10.ConclusionThe findings suggest that ADHD and cannabis use are related through a common vulnerability mutually exacerbating relationship where (a) ADHD symptoms present a risk factor for cannabis use onset, and (b) once cannabis use has begun, cannabis use and ADHD symptoms appear to mutually predict each other, suggesting a potential "spiral effect" that warrants attention.

items.title: Peripheral Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor Changes and Clinical Response to Electroconvulsive Therapy and Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in Major Depressive Disorder: A Systematic Review.
items.authors: Galindo CD, Jemar G, Osorio IC, Lopez A, Uribe Zapata M, Gonzalez Perez L, Villamil Montejo SD, Carvajal Angarita LA.

sections.text: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a leading contributor to the global burden of disease, and a substantial proportion of patients experience inadequate responses to conventional treatments. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), a key regulator of neuronal survival and synaptic plasticity, has been investigated as a potential biomarker of antidepressant response. However, its clinical relevance following brain stimulation remains uncertain. This systematic review evaluated changes in peripheral BDNF concentrations and their association with clinical outcomes following electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) and repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) in adults with MDD. The review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, and searches were conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE (Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online), PsycINFO, and LILACS (Latin America and the Caribbean Literature on Health Sciences). Study selection and data extraction were independently performed by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved through consensus or consultation with a third reviewer. Eleven studies met the eligibility criteria, including two randomized controlled trials and nine non-randomized investigations. Due to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, a meta-analysis was not performed, and findings were synthesized narratively. Peripheral BDNF responses varied across interventions, biological matrices, and sampling intervals. While many studies reported increased serum or plasma BDNF following ECT, others documented substantial clinical improvement without corresponding biomarker changes. Evidence following rTMS was less consistent, with insufficient data to establish a reliable association between BDNF changes and antidepressant response. Overall, peripheral BDNF changes did not consistently parallel clinical improvement, and current evidence does not support their use as a standalone biomarker of antidepressant response. Further adequately powered studies with standardized biomarker measurements and longitudinal clinical assessments are warranted.

items.title: Social Anxiety Modulates Default Mode Network Dysfunction and Working Memory Impairment During Social Media-Like Cue Distraction.
items.authors: Hu Y, Wei Z, Xu L, Becker B, Kou J.

sections.text: Recent studies have highlighted the adverse impact of social-media distractions on cognitive abilities, especially among individuals with anxiety who experience heightened apprehensions about providing immediate online social responses. Nevertheless, the investigation into the mechanism is scarce. In this fMRI study, 94 healthy adults completed a 2-back working memory (WM) task under three conditions using a between-subject design: social media-like cue distraction (e.g., WeChat), nonsocial digital distraction (e.g., browser), and no distraction. Data were analyzed using task-evoked activation analysis based on the general linear model (GLM) and functional network connectivity (FNC) analysis based on independent component analysis (ICA). Results showed that social media-like cue distraction impaired WM and altered posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) activity. Crucially, under the social media-like cue distraction condition, the brain-behavior relationship in the PCC was significantly moderated by trait social anxiety: higher social anxiety predicted a positive coupling between PCC activation and task accuracy, with decreased PCC activation associated with decreased accuracy; conversely, individuals with low social anxiety exhibited decreased PCC activation together with increased accuracy. This study is the first to demonstrate that cues resembling social media can specifically disrupt core brain regions of the default mode network (DMN; PCC) functions during WM tasks and that this neural response is influenced by individual levels of social anxiety.

items.title: SGLT-2 Inhibitors versus GLP-1 Receptor Agonists for Dementia and Depression in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Meta-Analysis.
items.authors: Pan R, Wang B, Li Y, Li H, Liang X, Zhang Y, Liu X, Huang X, Wang R, Ji H, Zhao Y.
items.journal: Diabetes, metabolic syndrome and obesity : targets and therapy

sections.text: The comparative effects of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) on dementia and depression risk in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remain unclear. We conducted a meta-analysis to directly compare the incidence of dementia and depression-related outcomes between users of these two drug classes. A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science from inception to June 1, 2026. Observational studies reporting quantifiable data on dementia or depression-related events in adults with T2DM were included. Detailed information on study design, age, demographic characteristics, eligibility criteria, outcome definitions, and outcome incidence was extracted. Data were pooled using a random-effects model to calculate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Sensitivity analyses involved sequential exclusion of individual studies. Prespecified subgroup analyses examined effect modifiers including geographic region, study design, age, and follow-up duration. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and the overall certainty of evidence and methodological rigor of this meta-analysis were evaluated using the AMSTAR 2 checklist. Thirteen observational studies comprising 1,055,315 participants were included. Compared with GLP-1RA users, SGLT-2i users had lower rates of all-cause dementia (OR 0.85, 95% CI 0.77-0.94; P = 0.001), vascular dementia (OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.71-0.80; P < 0.001), Alzheimer's disease (OR 0.76, 95% CI 0.72-0.79; P < 0.001), and composite depression-related outcomes (OR 0.76, 95% CI 0.67-0.88; P = 0.001), including suicide/self-harm (OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.60-0.80; P < 0.001) and depression/anxiety (OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.65-0.93; P = 0.006). Subgroup analyses revealed more pronounced differences in Asian populations (dementia: OR 0.86, 95% CI 0.75-0.99; I2 = 0%), European cohorts (depression: OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.54-0.84; I2 = 83%), and in studies that enrolled younger adults (minimum age 18 years, without an upper age restriction) (dementia: OR 0.79, 95% CI 0.76-0.81; I2 = 0%; depression: OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.54-0.84; I2 = 83%). In this meta-analysis of observational studies, SGLT-2i use was associated with lower rates of dementia and depression-related outcomes compared with GLP-1RA use in patients with T2DM. Age and geographic region may influence the observed associations. Future randomized controlled trials and studies reporting outcomes stratified by sex, socioeconomic status, and educational level are warranted.

items.title: Effectiveness, safety and therapeutic potential of medical cannabis across treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders: systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.authors: Guo D, Zong R, Ma Z, Lu F, Zhang Y, Zhang S, Yao Y, Bao Y, Zhang Y, Li X, Shi J, Jin M, Lu L, Liu L, Han Y.

sections.text: Medical cannabis has been suggested to have a therapeutic role in selected treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders. We analyzed the available evidence to assess the effectiveness and safety of these interventions in treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders. For this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched Web of Science, Cochrane, Embase, EBSCO, and PubMed for studies published between January 1, 1970, and April 25, 2026. We considered studies examining any type or formulation of medical cannabis in treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders. Primary outcomes were disorder-specific clinical improvement measures. Safety outcomes were adverse events, serious adverse events, and withdrawals due to adverse events. Evidence from studies was synthesized as equivalent odds ratios (eORs) for comparative outcomes and as pooled proportions for single-arm safety outcomes, via random-effects meta-analyses. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 for randomized trials, ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies, and structured quality assessment for case series and case reports, and certainty of evidence was assessed with GRADE. This study is registered with PROSPERO, CRD420251148868. 127 eligible studies were included, of which 32 studies involving 3645 participants contributed to meta-analysis. Meta-analysis showed improvement in drug-resistant epilepsy (eOR 0.50, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.34-0.72), refractory pain (eOR = 0.48, 95% CI = 0.30-0.78), and refractory multiple sclerosis spasticity (eOR = 0.22, 95% CI = 0.07-0.75). Evidence for psychiatric disorders was scarce. Small randomized trials reported improvement in PTSD-related nightmares and cannabis dependence after failed cessation. Uncontrolled studies reported improvements in hyperarousal, residual obsessive-compulsive symptoms, and refractory Tourette syndrome. Findings for treatment-resistant anxiety were inconsistent, and schizophrenia did not show a reliable therapeutic effect. Controlled analyses showed higher odds of any adverse events in drug-resistant epilepsy (eOR = 2.22, 95% CI = 1.52-3.23) and refractory multiple sclerosis (eOR = 1.89, 95% CI = 1.01-3.52), with higher odds of serious adverse events and withdrawals due to adverse events also observed in drug-resistant epilepsy. In single-arm and real-world studies, pooled proportions of any adverse events ranged from 15.5% in multiple sclerosis to 66.0% in Tourette syndrome, with substantial heterogeneity. Adjunctive pharmaceutical cannabidiol has the most consistent comparative evidence for reducing seizure frequency in selected drug-resistant epilepsy. Evidence for refractory pain and multiple sclerosis is heterogeneous and varies by clinical indication, cannabinoid formulation, and outcome definition. Evidence in treatment-resistant psychiatric disorders remains limited and is insufficient to support routine clinical recommendations. Further high-quality studies directly examining diagnosis-specific and formulation-specific effects, safety, and tolerability are needed. items.title: Prefrontal responses to negative emotional cognitive stimuli are associated with future suicide attempts in patients with mood disorders: a near-infrared spectroscopy study.
items.authors: Kamimura H, Matsuoka T, Okai H, Shimizu N, Harada S, Matsuo K.

sections.text: Early identification of suicide risk remains a critical challenge in psychiatry. Longitudinal evidence linking baseline brain responses to subsequent suicide attempts remains limited. In this exploratory prospective follow-up study, 29 patients with major depressive disorder or bipolar disorder underwent near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) during an emotional Stroop task at baseline; 22 completed the 6-month follow-up and were included in the analysis, five of whom attempted suicide. Baseline oxygenated hemoglobin (Oxy-Hb) responses during the threat-word condition were compared between patients with and without suicide attempts using Mann-Whitney U tests. The main exploratory NIRS measure was the mean normalized Oxy-Hb response across 15-45 s (periods b + c) in the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC); the corresponding left orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) measure was also examined. The follow-up attempt group showed higher baseline Oxy-Hb responses in the left DLPFC (U = 7.00, Holm-adjusted p = 0.022) and left OFC (U = 5.00, Holm-adjusted p = 0.020). Exploratory Spearman's rank correlations showed that baseline Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology scores were associated with the periods b + c NIRS measures in both regions, suggesting that baseline depressive symptom severity may have contributed to the observed group differences. These preliminary findings suggest that altered prefrontal hemodynamic responses during threat-related emotional interference may be associated with subsequent suicidal behavior. Larger prospective studies are required to replicate these findings and clarify their clinical relevance.

items.title: A pilot feasibility randomised controlled trial of an online cancer bereavement group.
items.authors: King L, Smith KV, Cole CL, Thompson EH.

sections.text: Bereavement following the death of a loved one from cancer presents unique challenges related to anticipatory stressors, caregiving demands, and the illness trajectory. Although online bereavement interventions may improve access to support, evidence for therapist-led online groups remains limited. This pilot randomised controlled trial evaluated the feasibility, acceptability and preliminary effectiveness of an online therapeutic group intervention for adults bereaved by cancer. In this longitudinal pilot RCT, adults bereaved by cancer were randomised to receive the intervention immediately or following a three-month wait-list period. The intervention comprised eight online group sessions delivered over 12 weeks, integrating trauma-informed cognitive behavioural therapy, compassion-focused therapy and psychoeducation. Primary outcomes were feasibility and acceptability. Secondary outcomes included prolonged grief, depression, anxiety, post-traumatic stress, self-compassion, and social disconnection, assessed at baseline, post-intervention, and three-month follow-up. Of 124 randomised participants, 100 (80.6%) commenced the allocated intervention and 97 contributed sufficient data for primary analyses. The study met pre-specified feasibility and acceptability criteria, although patterns of attrition differed according to trial stage. Non-commencement following allocation was higher in the immediate intervention groups (27.0 vs 11.5%) whereas withdrawal after intervention commencement was higher in the waitlist group (24.1% vs 10.9%). Exploratory between-group analyses suggested greater improvements in prolonged grief (d = -1.87), post-traumatic stress (d = -1.55), depression (d = -1.03), anxiety (d = -0.71), and self-compassion (d = 1.15) in the immediate intervention group compared with waitlist controls. No statistically significant between-group difference was observed for social disconnection (d = -0.49). Therapist-led online bereavement groups appear feasible and acceptable for adults bereaved by cancer and show promise for improving psychological outcomes. A fully powered RCT is warranted to establish efficacy.

items.title: Pandemic-Driven Mental Health Deterioration and Suicide Risk Among Health Science Students: A Longitudinal Cohort Study Unmasking the Trauma Multiplier Effect.
items.authors: Yusuf A, Aditya RS, Solikhah FK, AlMutairi RL, Fitryasari R, Ramadhan MP, Romadlona NA, Kurniawan SB, Kotijah S, Yanti IDS, Wibawa AP, Kartikasari D, Wijaya AB, Afandi AT, Al Razeeni DM, Widyaningtyas R.

sections.text: The COVID-19 pandemic precipitated an unprecedented mental health crisis among healthcare trainees-a population already burdened by academic and occupational stressors. items.title: Psychological Impact of COVID-19 on Nurses and Midwives in Albania: Fear, Anxiety and Predictors of Emotional Burden.
items.authors: Cake A, Ramosaçaj E, Simaku A, Bytyqi A, Zyberaj F.

sections.text: To examine associations between recalled COVID-19-related emotional burden, demographic, health and occupational factors, psychological support and trait anxiety among nurses and midwives in Albania. A quantitative cross-sectional analytical study using retrospective assessments of pandemic-related emotional experiences. Between March 2024 and May 2025, 1201 nurses and midwives from 17 public healthcare institutions in Albania completed structured questionnaires. Stratified random sampling was used. Descriptive analyses included the full cohort, while multivariable linear regression was conducted among 677 participants with complete trait anxiety and predictor data. Mean recalled anxiety, fear and distress scores were 6.53, 6.77 and 7.04, respectively, on 0-10 scales. Overall, 80.6% believed psychological support would have improved their coping. Fear showed the strongest emotional association with trait anxiety, followed by worry. Chronic disease and worsened perceived quality of life were associated with higher trait anxiety, whereas male gender, older age, greater professional experience and reported psychological support showed inverse associations. The adjusted regression model explained 55% of the variance in trait anxiety. Recalled pandemic-related fear and worry were associated with trait anxiety among nurses and midwives. Findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the retrospective assessment, cross-sectional design, and complete-case analysis. Nursing leadership should prioritize accessible, confidential psychological support and integrate workforce mental health into emergency preparedness strategies. This study identifies emotional and health-related factors associated with anxiety in the Albanian nursing and midwifery workforce, informing occupational health planning and future intervention research. The study was reported in accordance with the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) guidelines. The study involved nurses and midwives as research participants. Patients and members of the public were not involved in the study design, conduct, analysis or reporting.

items.title: Profound Hyperbilirubinemia During Severe Carbon Monoxide Poisoning and Subsequent Multiorgan Failure: A Case Report.
items.authors: Joma M, Zahran A, Karam A, Sawaf B, Sayeh W, Sodeman T, Alastal Y.

sections.text: Carbon monoxide poisoning is classically associated with neurologic and cardiovascular toxicity, while severe exposure may also cause systemic toxic-hypoxic injury. Profound direct-predominant hyperbilirubinemia without mechanical biliary obstruction is rarely described. We report a 55-year-old woman with alcohol use disorder, chronic tobacco use, COPD, and hepatic steatosis who presented with altered mental status and jaundice after suspected household carbon monoxide exposure. Her carboxyhemoglobin level was > 30%, and she required intubation, intensive care, vasopressor support, and three hyperbaric oxygen treatments. Initial testing showed total bilirubin of 23.1 mg/dL and direct bilirubin of 13.1 mg/dL, despite only mild AST elevation and near-normal ALT and alkaline phosphatase. Imaging showed hepatic steatosis and cholelithiasis without convincing biliary obstruction, and the documented workup for viral, autoimmune, metabolic, hemolytic, and vascular causes was unrevealing. Her liver dysfunction was considered multifactorial, with possible carbon monoxide-related toxic-hypoxic injury superimposed on underlying steatotic or alcohol-related liver vulnerability. After transient improvement, she developed coagulopathy, acute kidney injury, recurrent shock with clinical and imaging concern for acute cholecystitis, worsening hyperbilirubinemia peaking near 49-50 mg/dL, encephalopathy, respiratory failure, and multiorgan failure. Cholecystostomy yielded dark green bile without documented purulence, and aspirate cultures showed no growth; biliary sepsis was therefore not microbiologically confirmed. She died in the hospital after goals-of-care discussions. The initial bilirubin-predominant pattern was atypical for classic hypoxic hepatitis and may have reflected overlapping hepatic insults. This case emphasizes broad evaluation and cautious causal interpretation; it does not establish that carbon monoxide exposure alone caused the initial hyperbilirubinemia.

items.title: Adapted Massed Exposure Therapy Enhanced with MDMA for PTSD (aMETEMP): A randomized, double-masked protocol adapted for Veterans Affairs healthcare system.
items.authors: Morland LA, Chargin B, Rothbaum B, Maples-Keller JL, Wachsman T, Norman SB, Adams SN, Perivoliotis D, Alam A, Stauffer CS, Angkaw AC, Marquez V, Woolley J, Kopelman JM, Schnurr PP.

sections.text: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) remains prevalent and disabling, especially among veterans, with a substantial proportion failing to achieve remission following first-line evidence-based trauma-focused psychotherapies. 3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) is hypothesized to enhance psychotherapy outcomes through effects on fear extinction, cognitive flexibility, and emotional engagement, and is being studied as a promising augmentation strategy for PTSD psychotherapy. There is limited research combining MDMA with evidence-based PTSD treatment. MDMA-assisted psychotherapy trials to date have also been limited by lack of an active comparator and functional unmasking. We describe the methodology of an ongoing randomized, double-masked, pilot trial evaluating massed prolonged exposure (PE) therapy enhanced with MDMA for PTSD (aMETEMP), adapted for a U.S. Veterans Affairs outpatient setting. Up to 20 veterans with PTSD in the VA will receive a 6-8hr in-person MDMA dosing session (randomized dose 35 mg - 125 mg) integrated with a 3-week massed exposure protocol. The remaining visits are virtual and include PE sessions and sessions to prepare for and process the MDMA session (28-30hrs total over 11 visits), with the use of telehealth intended to improve access and ease patient burden. After treating the first 4 participants, who were fully informed of the trial design, we switched to using an incomplete disclosure strategy (not disclosing the number of treatment arms or specific possible doses) to further improve masking. Primary outcomes include PTSD severity using the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5, safety, feasibility, and masking success. Findings are intended to provide preliminary descriptive information regarding feasibility, safety/tolerability, masking integrity, and symptom-change signals for aMETEMP with incomplete disclosure in a large outpatient healthcare system. items.title: A stacking machine learning model for identifying comorbid anxiety disorder in children and adolescents with functional abdominal pain disorders.
items.authors: Wu W, Ye Q, Lin X, Li S, Wang S, Liu X.

sections.text: Comorbid anxiety disorder is common in children and adolescents with functional abdominal pain disorders, but clinically usable risk-stratification tools integrating abdominal pain, psychosocial, school-related, and family-level information remain limited. In this observational predictive modeling study, children and adolescents aged 7-18 years with Rome IV-defined functional abdominal pain disorders were evaluated between December 2021 and December 2025. Participants were randomly allocated at a 7:3 ratio into training and internal validation cohorts using stratified sampling by anxiety status. Candidate predictors included demographic, abdominal pain-related, somatic, psychosocial, school-related, and family-level variables. After LASSO-based feature selection, four prespecified base learners-explainable boosting machine, calibrated support vector machine, random forest, and CatBoost-were combined using an L2-penalized logistic regression stacking meta-learner. Performance was assessed using discrimination, threshold-dependent metrics, calibration, decision curve analysis, learner diversity, and SHAP-based interpretability. Among 629 eligible patients, 210 (33.4%) had comorbid anxiety disorder. The training cohort included 440 patients, and the validation cohort included 189 patients, with similar anxiety prevalence in both cohorts. Clinically relevant correlates of anxiety included older age, longer symptom duration, higher pain frequency, night-time awakening, pain temporally associated with stressful events, higher SDSC and CSI-24 scores, higher parental GAD-7 score, and greater school absence. In out-of-fold training estimates, the stacking model achieved an AUC of 0.831 and a Brier score of 0.151. In the validation cohort, it showed the highest numerical performance among candidate models, with an AUC of 0.846 (95% CI, 0.789-0.894), accuracy of 0.788, sensitivity of 0.762, specificity of 0.802, F1 score of 0.706, and Brier score of 0.146. Decision curve analysis suggested potential clinical utility across selected threshold ranges. SHAP analysis identified school absence, parental GAD-7 score, CSI-24 score, pain-stress association, symptom duration, pain frequency, SDSC score, age, and night-time awakening as leading contributors to the final model output. A stacking machine learning model integrating clinical, psychosocial, school-related, and family-level variables showed acceptable internal-validation performance for identifying comorbid anxiety disorder in children and adolescents with functional abdominal pain disorders. External validation is needed before clinical implementation.

items.title: From single pathways to holistic networks: unraveling the multimechanistic actions of acupuncture in depression.
items.authors: Quan S, Xu W, Du H, Xu Z, Zhao T, Zhao M, Lin X, Chen X.

sections.text: Depression is a globally prevalent mental disorder; however, current pharmacological treatments are limited by a delayed onset of action and significant adverse effects. As a safe and effective non-pharmacological therapy, acupuncture demonstrates unique advantages in treating mild to moderate depression. Its antidepressant mechanisms are multifaceted. Primarily, acupuncture mitigates neuroinflammation by inhibiting classical signaling pathways (e.g., nuclear factor kappa B/NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3), modulating microglial polarization, and restoring cytokine homeostasis. Furthermore, it enhances neuroplasticity by upregulating brain-derived neurotrophic factor expression, improving synaptic plasticity, and promoting adult neurogenesis. At the cellular level, acupuncture exerts neuroprotective effects by suppressing apoptotic cascades associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and endoplasmic reticulum stress, regulating autophagic balance, and restoring neuronal excitability. Systemically, it ameliorates metabolic dysregulation by optimizing cerebral energy metabolism, modulating gut microbiota composition, and reinforcing intestinal barrier integrity. Additionally, acupuncture effectively alleviates comorbid pain by modulating peripheral nociceptive signaling and central pain-emotion feedback loops. These synergistic effects across multiple systems and targets may together ameliorate the pathophysiological alterations associated with depression. Despite these advances, current research faces challenges, including the translational gap between animal models and clinical pathology, as well as an insufficient investigation of multi-mechanism interactions. Future efforts should focus on developing clinically relevant models, integrating multi-omics technologies, conducting high-quality clinical trials, and exploring biomarker-guided personalized treatments to advance the scientific and standardized application of acupuncture for depression.

items.title: The relationship between sleep problems and well-being among Chinese children: a moderated mediation model with anxiety as mediator and resilience as moderator.
items.authors: Ding J, Hou X, Dou G.

sections.text: Prior research has shown that well-being is a key factor in children's developmental outcomes. However, the factors that relate to children's well-being are still unclear, especially among Chinese populations. This research investigated the relationship between sleep problems and the well-being of children in China, specifically testing (1) whether sleep problems were associated with well-being, (2) whether anxiety may serve as a mediator, and (3) whether resilience may moderate this association. A total of 606 Chinese children (53.3% girls; mean age = 11.09 years) participated in the present study using a cross-sectional design by completing self-report instruments, including the Athens Insomnia Scale, the Oxford Happiness Questionnaire, the Anxiety subscale of the Depression Anxiety Stress Scale, and the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale. Pearson correlations and a moderated mediation analysis using PROCESS Model 58 with 5,000 bootstrap samples were conducted, controlling for age. (1) There was a significant negative correlation between sleep problems and well-being (r = -0.39, p < 0.001). (2) After controlling for age, anxiety mediated this association. (3) Resilience moderated this association. Specifically, the indirect effect was stronger in the high-resilience group (indirect effect = -0.15, 95% CI = [-0.23, -0.08]) than in the low-resilience group (indirect effect = -0.05, 95% CI = [-0.09, -0.03]). These findings provide preliminary evidence on how sleep problems are associated with well-being among Chinese children. They also suggest that anxiety and resilience may be relevant for future intervention studies, although longitudinal and experimental designs are needed to test whether targeting these factors can improve mental health.

items.title: Dose-related depressive symptoms and suicidal ideation during cabergoline therapy in an adolescent with macroprolactinoma.
items.authors: Malik S, Al Harrasi A, Al Kiyumi MI, Al Kiyumi MH.

sections.text: Cabergoline is the preferred medical treatment for prolactinomas in children and adolescents because of its efficacy in reducing prolactin concentrations and tumor size. Although dopamine agonists are generally well tolerated, neuropsychiatric adverse effects have been reported, with depressive symptoms and suicidal ideation less frequently described. We report a 15-year-old girl with macroprolactinoma who developed low mood, emotional dysregulation, crying spells, reduced appetite, sleep-wake disturbance, loss of interest in previously enjoyable activities, and passive suicidal thoughts after cabergoline was increased to 1 mg twice weekly. She had no previous psychiatric history, major psychosocial stressor, manic symptoms, or psychotic features. Psychiatric assessment identified moderate depressive symptoms, with a Patient Health Questionnaire-9 score of 11. Cabergoline was reduced to 0.75 mg twice weekly because of the close temporal relationship between dose escalation and symptom onset. Her psychiatric symptoms almost completely resolved within a few days, while prolactin remained controlled. The temporal association, apparent dose relationship, and rapid improvement following dose reduction suggest a cabergoline-associated neuropsychiatric adverse reaction. Clinicians should monitor mood and suicidal ideation during dopamine agonist therapy, particularly after dose escalation and in adolescents.

items.title: Correlation between chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and comorbidities-a systematic analysis integrating global burden of disease and mendelian randomization study.
items.authors: Feng H, Jiao C, Lv W, Zheng R.

sections.text: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) frequently coexists with multiple comorbidities. However, the long-term trends, regional disparities, and potential causal relationships in the global burden of these comorbidities remain to be systematically elucidated. This study aimed to characterize the disease burden of common comorbidities in patients with COPD and to assess the potential causal relationships between these comorbidities and COPD. This study integrated data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 (GBD 2023) and conducted two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses. Based on GBD data from 1990 to 2023, we performed descriptive burden assessment, Das Gupta decomposition, Bayesian age-period-cohort modelling, exploratory correlation analysis, and formal age-interaction regression. Using summary statistics from the FinnGen consortium, we evaluated bidirectional genetic associations between COPD and various comorbidities primarily via the inverse variance weighted (IVW) method with false discovery rate (FDR) correction for multiple comparisons. The comorbidities of focus included asthma, anxiety disorders, major depressive disorder, pulmonary hypertension, hypertensive heart disease, ischemic heart disease, musculoskeletal disorders, osteoporosis, and respiratory tract cancers. The absolute burden of comorbidities in COPD continued to increase, albeit driven by distinct factors. Population aging and growth were identified as the primary drivers for the rising burden of several COPD comorbidities, such as ischemic heart disease and musculoskeletal disorders. Significant regional inequalities were observed in disease distribution: high Socio-demographic Index (SDI) regions bore a heavier burden of musculoskeletal and mental disorders, whereas middle and low SDI regions exhibited more pronounced mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) attributable to ischemic heart disease. Formal interaction models demonstrated significant age heterogeneity in the ecological associations between COPD prevalence and all eight comorbidities after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (all q ≤0.028). MR analyses provided evidence supporting bidirectional genetic associations between COPD and specific comorbidities. Genetically predicted COPD was significantly associated with an increased risk of asthma and depression (FDR <0.05), and conversely, genetic susceptibility to asthma and depression was associated with a higher risk of developing COPD (FDR <0.05). The comorbidity patterns between COPD and its key concomitant conditions are influenced by multiple factors, including demographic structure, regional development levels, and shared biological mechanisms. Our findings underscore the necessity of shifting from a single-disease management model towards integrated care strategies that emphasize comorbidity screening and holistic patient management.

Genetically predicted COPD was significantly associated with an increased risk of asthma and depression (FDR <0.05), and conversely, genetic susceptibility to asthma and depression was associated with a higher risk of developing COPD (FDR <0.05). The comorbidity patterns between COPD and its key concomitant conditions are influenced by multiple factors, including demographic structure, regional development levels, and shared biological mechanisms. Our findings underscore the necessity of shifting from a single-disease management model towards integrated care strategies that emphasize comorbidity screening and holistic patient management.

items.title: Digital pathways to self-harm: Modafinil-induced mania and AI-assisted operationalization of suicidal intent in a law student: a case report.
items.authors: Manea MM, Moise-Crintea A, Singalievici PA, Muntean MI, Coman HG.

sections.text: Modafinil is a wakefulness-promoting (eugeroic) agent increasingly used off-label for cognitive enhancement. Although generally regarded as having a favorable psychiatric safety profile, it can precipitate manic or hypomanic episodes in vulnerable individuals, and the boundary between a self-limited substance-induced episode and the unmasking of an underlying mood disorder is not always clear at presentation. We report the case of a 20-year-old female law student admitted to the emergency unit after a suicide attempt by polypharmacy overdose during escalating off-label modafinil use. A notable feature was her use of an artificial intelligence (AI) conversational platform to inform about the preparation of the attempt: the AI did not generate her suicidal motivation but contributed to operationalizing an already-formed intent. The acute presentation was characterized by logorhoea, affective expansiveness, and behavioral disinhibition, initially consistent with a substance-induced manic episode. Over the three-month follow-up, however, subsyndromal hypomanic features persisted after discontinuation of modafinil and after withdrawal of a serotonergic antidepressant, while the patient was maintained on a mood stabilizer - raising the possibility that modafinil acted as a precipitant unmasking an underlying bipolar diathesis. This case illustrates modafinil's potential to precipitate affective destabilization in a high-achieving young person under sustained academic pressure, and the difficulty of distinguishing a transient substance-induced episode from an emerging bipolar-spectrum disorder without longitudinal follow-up. It also highlights an emerging risk: the role of large language models (LLMs) in operationalizing - rather than originating - suicidal intent. The case underscores the need for careful psychiatric screening before prescribing wakefulness-promoting agents, for continued longitudinal monitoring, and for attention to patients' interactions with AI platforms during crisis assessment.

items.title: Associations Between Psychological Factors, Routine Hematological and Biochemical Indicators, and Non-Suicidal Self-Injury Among University Students: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: Lv J, Du Y, Han Y, Yang X, Chen J, Liu X, Sun Y, Wang Y, Li N, Liu J, Yao D, Wang R, Qin H, Cao J.

sections.text: Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is a major mental health concern among university students. Although psychological risk factors for NSSI have been extensively studied, the potential contribution of routinely available hematological and biochemical indicators remains unclear. This study examined their associations with NSSI and their incremental value beyond psychological factors. This cross-sectional study included 1,661 university students who completed campus psychological screening and routine health examinations. NSSI status was defined as an NSSI total score greater than zero. Psychological variables included depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, sleep problems, impulsivity, attentional control, cognitive emotion regulation strategies, and problematic internet use. Associations between routine indicators and NSSI severity were examined using Spearman correlations, while logistic regression models evaluated associations with NSSI status after adjustment for demographic and psychological factors. Five-fold cross-validation was used to compare predictive performance across demographic, routine indicator, psychological, and combined models. Among the 1,661 participants, 244 (14.69%) were classified as having NSSI. Several routine indicators, including AST, ALT, red blood cell count, uric acid, hemoglobin, and hematocrit, showed weak correlations with NSSI total scores after FDR correction. However, no routine hematological or biochemical indicator remained significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction in either adjusted logistic regression model. The psychological model showed substantially better predictive performance than demographic or routine indicator models, and adding routine indicators did not improve prediction (AUC: 0.796 vs. 0.787). Routine hematological and biochemical indicators showed weak associations with NSSI severity but provided limited incremental value beyond psychological factors for identifying NSSI among university students. Psychological assessment remains an important component of NSSI screening, whereas routine laboratory data did not show additional incremental value in this sample.

items.title: Psychological and Material Pathways to Adolescent Well-Being: The Mediating Role of Depressive Symptoms.
items.authors: Liang C, Lv Z, Hu Y.

sections.text: Against the backdrop of rising family educational expenditures and increasing prevalence of adolescent depression, this study examined the parallel mediating effects of psychological and material pathways on adolescent well-being. This study analyzed data from 1151 adolescents aged 10-19 years in the 2022 China Family Panel Studies (CFPS). A parallel multiple mediation model was used to examine two pathways: a psychological pathway in which future orientation is associated with well-being via depressive symptoms, and a material pathway in which educational investment is associated with well-being via depressive symptoms. Indirect effects and differences between pathways were tested using bias-corrected bootstrapping with 5000 resamples. Future orientation was significantly negatively associated with depressive symptoms (β = -0.257, p < 0.001), with a significant indirect effect on well-being via depressive symptoms (indirect effect = 0.167, 95% CI [0.107, 0.238]). Family educational investment was not significantly associated with depressive symptoms (β = -0.036, p = 0.203), and its indirect effect was non-significant. The difference between the two indirect effects was significant (Δ = 0.157, 95% CI [0.101, 0.231]), indicating that the indirect effect via the psychological pathway was stronger than that via the material pathway. These findings provide preliminary evidence that future orientation, as a psychological resource, is associated with lower depressive symptoms and higher hedonic well-being among Chinese adolescents. However, owing to the cross-sectional design and measurement limitations (eg, a single-item measure of eudaimonic well-being), the results should be interpreted as statistical associations rather than causal pathways. They do not justify broad claims that challenge human capital theory or provide strong support for hope theory; rather, they suggest that psychological and material pathways may differ in their associations with adolescent mental health. Future longitudinal and, where feasible, experimental or intervention research using independent measures is needed.

items.title: Genetic risk of psychopathology predicts environmental risk.
items.authors: Socrates A, Baldwin JR, Murray RM, O'Reilly PF, Pingault JB.

sections.text: The exposome has been conceptualised as the sum of environmental exposures across the life course, but these exposures are unlikely to be independent of genetic influences. We tested whether nine polygenic scores for psychiatric, cognitive, personality and comparison traits were associated with 49 environmental risk factors in 307,493 UK Biobank participants. Across 441 models, 212 associations remained significant after false discovery rate correction. ADHD, educational attainment, major depression, schizophrenia and bipolar disorder polygenic scores showed the broadest profiles, but the pattern of association differed substantially across traits. Schizophrenia and bipolar disorder polygenic scores were most strongly associated with interpersonal adversity and victimisation, major depression and ADHD with perception/subjectivity, and educational attainment with socioeconomic circumstances, health and health behaviour. Schizophrenia, major depression, ADHD, bipolar disorder and neuroticism polygenic scores were also more strongly associated with perception/subjectivity factors than with objective/non-perception factors. These findings show that genetic liability is associated with a broad but structured portion of the psychiatric exposome, spanning social adversity, behaviour, socioeconomic circumstances and subjective experience. They further suggest that the widespread influence of genetics on the exposome may partly reflect genetically influenced perception of environmental risk as well as differences in environmental exposure.

items.title: Exploring the Association of Fear, Mental Health, and Lifestyle with Insomnia: A Machine Learning Approach among University Students.
items.authors: Khademi S, Saebipour MR, Saadatfar H, Riahi SM.

sections.text: The aim of this study was to identify key predictors of insomnia among university students, focusing on psychological, behavioral, and lifestyle factors. The study also aimed to explore the role of machine learning in identifying insomnia-related patterns and informing personalized intervention strategies. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 576 students from universities in Birjand during the 2023-2024 academic year. Machine learning methods, including Random Forest, Decision Tree, and SHAP analysis, were used for feature importance analysis and knowledge extraction. Self-reported questionnaires revealed that fear of not falling asleep particularly in the late hours and stress were the most significant predictors of insomnia. Anxiety, poor sleep hygiene, and depression were also strongly associated with insomnia. Other associated factors included financial and family concerns, bedtime, wake-up time, sleep duration, and social media usage. Machine learning models further highlighted these factors, with those showing poor sleep hygiene and high anxiety levels being more likely to experience insomnia. The findings underscore the complex relationship between mental health issues and sleep disorders, particularly insomnia, in university students. The results also suggest a bidirectional relationship between insomnia, anxiety, depression, and stress. The use of machine learning showed potential for identifying insomnia-related patterns and informing personalized intervention strategies. These results highlight the need for effective strategies to address insomnia in students, particularly in light of the growing stressors faced in academic and personal life. However, due to the cross-sectional design, causal inferences cannot be drawn.

items.title: Implementing "Community-based approach for lowering stress through mindfulness in Chicago" (CALM-Chicago) for depression and hypertension: Study protocol of a proof-of-concept trial.
items.authors: Carroll AJ, Davis P, Reed LR, Ellis A, Kandula NR, Kho AN, Youmans QR, Maletich CM, Huffman MD, Smith JD, Burnett-Zeigler IE.

sections.text: Community-based mental health interventions hold potential to reach communities who are less likely to engage in traditional clinic-based services. Partnering with community members and organizations to develop a community-informed approach increases the likelihood of successful implementation of these interventions. We will evaluate the effectiveness and implementation of an adapted mindfulness-based stress reduction intervention among Black/African American adults with comorbid depression and hypertension. This trial is a single-arm, type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation study. We will recruit Black/African American adults (≥18 years) with elevated depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 scores ≥10) and a self-reported diagnosis of hypertension. All participants will be enrolled in an 8-week mindfulness-based stress reduction program that has been adapted for Black/African American adults, heart health, and community-based delivery. Study participants will complete surveys at baseline and at 4 weeks and 8 weeks post-baseline; blood pressure readings before and after the first and final mindfulness sessions; and a post-intervention focus group. We will also recruit community members to a community advisory board to advise on trial execution, challenges, implementation, and evaluation. Primary effectiveness outcomes include effect sizes of changes in depressive symptoms (Patient Health Questionnaire-9 scores) and systolic blood pressure from baseline to 8 weeks. The primary implementation outcome of implementation acceptability, appropriateness, feasibility will be assessed using mixed qualitative-quantitative methods. Successful completion of this trial will provide preliminary evidence for the effectiveness of mindfulness for improving depression and blood pressure control as well as the implementation of community-based mindfulness programs. ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06987799).

items.title: Self-Reported ADHD Among Portuguese Medical Residents: Medication Use, Psychiatric Comorbidities, and Perceived Professional Impact.
items.authors: Azenha JP, Cândido M, Domingos JT, Medinas RL, Sousa DE.

sections.text: Background ADHD is increasingly recognised in medical trainees, yet data from Portuguese residency programmes are lacking. Objectives This study aimed to assess the proportion of self-reported diagnosed or suspected ADHD among Portuguese medical residents, characterise medication use patterns, identify psychiatric comorbidities, and evaluate perceived professional impact. Methods Cross-sectional, observational study based on an anonymous online questionnaire distributed to medical residents across multiple Portuguese training centres between March and June 2026 (n = 225). ADHD symptoms were assessed using the Portuguese version of the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale version 1.1 (ASRS-v1.1). Results A total of 225 residents completed the questionnaire. Diagnosed or suspected ADHD was self-reported by 37.3% (n = 84) of participants. Among this group, 66.7% (n = 56) reported that ADHD was first identified after commencing residency, and 56.0% (n = 47) reported no formal evaluation. Medication use was reported by 25.8% (n = 58). Among medication users, 32.8% (19/58) reported obtaining medication from a colleague or friend, through self-prescription, or without a formal prescription. Psychiatric comorbidities were significantly more prevalent in the self-reported ADHD group than in participants not reporting ADHD (61/84, 72.6% vs 69/141, 48.9%; p < 0.001). Professional impact was perceived as negative by 83.3% (n = 70) of this group. Conclusions Portuguese medical residents reported high rates of diagnosed or suspected ADHD, frequent medication use outside conventional prescribing pathways, and substantial perceived professional impairment. These findings highlight the need for structured diagnostic pathways and institutional support within residency training programmes.

items.title: Parental adverse childhood experiences, parenting styles, and stress: a comparison of child psychopathology diagnostic groups.
items.authors: Pfaff K, Lion S, Hussong J, Honecker-Gebauer H, Möhler E.
items.journal: Frontiers in child and adolescent psychiatry

sections.text: Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are associated with long-term impairments in physical and mental health and may influence the development of the next generation. Although parental ACEs have been linked to parenting difficulties and increased parental stress, their role across child psychiatric disorders remains unclear. This cross-sectional observational study examined associations between parental ACEs, parenting style, parental stress, and child psychopathology in a sample of 76 children and adolescents (aged 6-17 years) across three diagnostic groups: ADHD (n = 29), internalizing disorders (n = 32), and functional incontinence (n = 15). Parents completed the ACE-D, EEI, ESF, and CBCL 6-18R. Descriptively, mothers reported higher mean ACE scores than fathers (1.5 vs. 0.9). Parental ACE scores correlated with child externalizing symptoms (ρ = .386, p < .01) and parental stress (ρ = .257, p < .05), but not with internalizing symptoms. Parenting style differed between groups, with parents of children with ADHD reporting greater strictness than parents of children with internalizing disorders. No direct association between ACE scores and parenting style was found. The overall group difference in parental stress was significant, but no post-hoc group comparison remained significant. Love/appreciation was negatively associated with both symptom dimensions and parental stress. Regression analysis identified externalizing symptoms (β = .454, p < .001) and role restriction (β = .336, p < .01) as significant predictors of parental stress (adjusted R2 = .46). As both, role restriction and parental stress are subscales of one questionnaire, this association may reflect common-method variance. Parental ACEs are associated with child externalizing symptoms and heightened parental stress, but showed no direct relationship with parenting style, suggesting ACEs operate via different risk factors. In the multiple regression model, parental ACE scores were no longer significantly associated with parental stress once child externalizing symptoms and role restriction were taken into account. These findings underscore the relevance of positive parenting, child externalizing symptoms, and perceived role restriction in understanding parental stress. Routine ACE assessment may identify at-risk families and inform interventions targeting parental stress and positive parent-child relationships.

items.title: Unmasking neurodevelopmental assessment: the potential role for virtual reality as a multimodal clinical adjunct.
items.authors: Goh CCW, Rizzo AS.

sections.text: Children with neurodevelopmental conditions (NDCs), particularly attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD), may alter or suppress aspects of their behavioral presentation in structured social and assessment contexts. This phenomenon, often described as masking or camouflaging, can complicate clinical interpretation and may contribute to delayed or incomplete identification in some individuals. Immersive virtual reality (VR) offers a potentially useful complementary assessment context by combining ecologically relevant task demands with continuous measurement of cognitive performance and objective metrics such as gaze and motor behavior that are less accessible to deliberate control. We propose that immersion in VR may also reduce the salience of the immediate social audience and thereby lessen some forms of assessment-context distortion, although this mechanism has not yet been directly tested. Emerging studies demonstrate that VR-derived motor and gaze measures can distinguish group-level neurodevelopmental profiles and provide information beyond conventional task performance. While these measures are not currently diagnostically specific, they may serve as adjunctive sources of behavioral information to support clinical decisions. Drawing on independent research and clinical implementation experience, this Perspective examines the empirical basis for VR-enabled assessment, proposes testable mechanisms by which it might reduce contextual distortion for children with NDCs, and considers the validation, ethical, accessibility, cultural, and implementation requirements necessary for responsible clinical use.

items.title: Fear of COVID-19 and PTSD symptoms in adolescents: the mediating role of meaning in life and the moderating role of gender.
items.authors: Lv W, Wang Y, Long Z, Fei S, Song J, Chen W.

sections.text: The COVID-19 pandemic and related restrictions were associated with substantial mental health burdens among adolescents, including PTSD symptoms. Meaning in life may explain the association between fear of COVID-19 and PTSD symptoms, and this association may differ by gender. This study examined the association between fear of COVID-19 and PTSD symptoms among Chinese adolescents, tested the distinct indirect effects of Presence of Meaning and Search for Meaning, and evaluated whether gender moderated the second-stage paths from both meaning dimensions to PTSD. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 1,291 middle school students recruited through convenience sampling. Participants completed the FCV-19S, PCL-C, MLQ, and a demographic survey. The sample included 656 females (50.8%) and 635 males (49.2%), aged 11-18 years (M = 14.13, SD = 1.35). Analyses were conducted using IBM SPSS 27.0 and PROCESS macro version 4.1; age was included as a covariate in every mediation and moderated mediation equation. Fear of COVID-19 was positively correlated with PTSD symptoms (r = 0.31, p < 0.001). After controlling for age, the indirect effect was significant through Presence of Meaning (B = 0.059, 95% CI [0.031, 0.089]) but not Search for Meaning (B = 0.005, 95% CI [-0.001, 0.015]); this pattern held in the parallel model (Presence: B = 0.060, 95% CI [0.032, 0.092]; Search: B = -0.002, 95% CI [-0.009, 0.004]). Gender moderated the second-stage Presence-PTSD path (B = -0.159, p = 0.044; stronger among females) and the Search-PTSD path (B = -0.231, p = 0.016; negative among females but not males). In age-adjusted models, Presence of Meaning, but not Search for Meaning, showed a significant indirect association. Gender moderated the second-stage paths from both dimensions to PTSD, but the overall indirect effects did not differ by gender. These findings support distinguishing having meaning from seeking meaning; longitudinal research is needed to test causal or intervention implications.

items.title: Mindfulness and anxiety among young family caregivers: the mediating roles of psychological flexibility and self-compassion.
items.authors: Liu Y, Zhong S, Yang C.

sections.text: During critical developmental periods, young family caregivers frequently take on unpaid caregiving for family members who are physically ill, have disabilities, or have mental health conditions. Ongoing caregiving pressure may be associated with a greater risk of anxiety and poorer mental health. Psychological flexibility and self-compassion reflect distinct but interrelated psychological processes involved in responding to stress and may help characterize the association between mindfulness and anxiety. Accordingly, among young family caregivers, this study examined the association between mindfulness and anxiety and whether psychological flexibility and self-compassion function as sequential mediators. A total of 485 young family caregivers aged 15-24 were recruited from three prefecture-level cities in Hunan Province, China. All participants completed measures of mindfulness, psychological flexibility, self-compassion, and anxiety. Structural equation modeling was used to examine the hypothesized relationships, and the serial indirect effect was examined using 5,000 bootstrap resamples with bias-corrected 95% confidence intervals. Higher mindfulness was associated with greater psychological flexibility and self-compassion and lower anxiety; greater psychological flexibility was associated with greater self-compassion and lower anxiety, while greater self-compassion was associated with lower anxiety. The hypothesized serial indirect association from mindfulness to anxiety through psychological flexibility and self-compassion was significant (β = -0.128, 95% CI [-0.167, -0.096]). The findings support the relevance of the stress process model to young family caregiving and suggest that anxiety is associated not only with caregiving burden, but also with how caregiving-related stress is processed and how individuals respond to their own distress. These findings point to the potential value of considering internal psychological resources alongside the family caregiving context and support from schools, communities, and service systems.

items.title: Virtual reality-based intervention in forensic mental health services: a feasibility study of implementation, acceptability, and clinical outcomes.
items.authors: Escuder-Romeva G, Vorstenbosch E, Olivé-Albitzur AE, Tre-Ortega V, Sanz-Heras R, Luna-Rodríguez E, Civit-Ramírez M, Brophy-Palma MC, Pérez-Sánchez EJ, Del Prado-Sánchez N, Ribas-Siñol M.

sections.text: This study evaluated the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary clinical outcomes of an immersive virtual reality (VR)-based relaxation program implemented as part of routine care in adult and juvenile forensic mental healthcare settings. A feasibility study was conducted in two forensic mental healthcare services: an adult prison-based rehabilitation unit (UHRPI; n = 21) and a juvenile justice treatment unit (UTJJ; n = 8). The 12-week study comprised a four-week pre-intervention phase, a four-week intervention phase including eight VR sessions, and a four-week post-intervention phase. Feasibility, comprising service-user acceptability and professional usability, was the primary outcome. Secondary exploratory outcomes included physiological measures (blood pressure and heart rate), state anxiety (STAI-State), and subjective emotional states assessed immediately before and after each VR session using visual analog scales (VAS). Participant-level behavioral indicators extracted from institutional clinical records were summarized descriptively. Linear mixed-effects models were used to analyze repeated physiological and VAS measures, whereas state anxiety was analyzed using paired-samples t-tests. Acceptability and usability were high in both settings, and the intervention was generally well tolerated. In the UHRPI, significant reductions were observed in systolic blood pressure, heart rate, and state anxiety; no significant physiological or anxiety changes were observed in the UTJJ. In both settings, stress and anxiety decreased and relaxation and perceived connection with nature increased immediately following VR sessions, whereas changes in happiness and craving reached significance in only one setting. Participant-level behavioral indicators showed descriptive reductions in several indicators across study phases, with patterns differing between settings. The VR-based relaxation program was feasible, acceptable, and well integrated into routine forensic mental healthcare. The intervention was associated with improvements in immediate emotional responses across both settings and with favorable physiological changes in adults. Descriptive behavioral findings suggest potential benefits that warrant further investigation. Larger controlled studies with predefined clinical and safety outcomes are needed to determine effectiveness, establish causal effects, and evaluate long-term implementation.

items.authors: Rioux C, Waldron ME, Fulp DC.

sections.text: Data from the Multi-Sensitivity Study includes sociodemographic factors, sensory processing sensitivity (a.k.a, highly sensitive personality), the Adult Sensory Profile, rejection sensitivity, mental health (distress, well-being, alcohol/cannabis use), discrimination, and social support (informational, emotional, and companionship). The data (n = 617, United States) was collected through an online cross-sectional self-report survey on Prolific. The Prolific representative sample option was used, stratifying based on sex, age, and ethnicity. The primary and processed data are available on OSF and have reuse potential for clinical and social psychology research, psychometrics research, methodological research on crowdsourcing for participant recruitment, and for use in statistics courses.
