items.title: Influence of physical activity and sedentary behaviour on anxiety and depression among breast cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy: a longitudinal cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Grupińska J, Jurys T, Grajek M, Budzyń M, Malchrowicz-Mośko E.
items.journal: Reports of practical oncology and radiotherapy : journal of Greatpoland Cancer Center in Poznan and Polish Society of Radiation Oncology

sections.text: Breast cancer is most commonly associated with psychological distress, particularly anxiety and depression. While physical activity has been shown to mitigate these symptoms, sedentary behaviour may contribute to their worsening. We aimed to assess changes in symptoms of anxiety/depression over time and to examine their associations with physical activity and sedentary behaviour in women undergoing chemotherapy. Sixty women aged 40-80 years with histopathologically confirmed breast cancer after surgery were consecutively recruited using purposive sampling. Each participant was assessed twice: before initiation of chemotherapy and six weeks later. Physical activity and sedentary behaviour were measured using the Polish version of the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ-L), whereas symptoms of anxiety and depression were assessed with the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). Statistical analyses included paired tests and correlation analyses (Spearman's coefficients). Symptoms of anxiety/depression significantly decreased between assessments (p = 0.001 and p = 0.031, respectively). Higher daily walking time was inversely correlated with depression (ρ = -0.399, p = 0.002) and anxiety (ρ = -0.317, p = 0.014). Conversely, sedentary time was positively associated with both depression (ρ = 0.292, p = 0.023) and anxiety (ρ = 0.284, p = 0.028). No significant associations were found between moderate-to-vigorous physical activity and psychological symptoms. Among clinical factors, only age and HER2 status showed notable influence. In this sample, higher levels of walking were associated with lower anxiety and depression scores, while greater sedentary time was linked with higher symptom levels. These associations suggest that encouraging accessible physical activity and reducing sedentary behaviour may represent useful components of supportive oncological care.

RiboMeth-Sequencing Reveals Selective Ribosomal RNA 2'-O-Methylation Changes in the Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex of Subjects With Major Depressive Disorder.
items.authors: Verma AK, Roy B, Prall K, Dwivedi Y.

sections.text: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is associated with widespread molecular abnormalities in the brain; however, the contribution of ribosome-centered regulatory mechanisms remains poorly understood. Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) 2'-O-methylation (Nm) is the most abundant and evolutionarily conserved RNA modification and has emerged as a determinant of ribosome heterogeneity and translational control. However, the rRNA Nm landscape has not been examined in psychiatric illness. Here, we used RiboMeth-seq to map site-specific rRNA Nm in the MDD brain. RiboMeth-seq was performed in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex of individuals with MDD (n = 17) and matched nonpsychiatric control subjects (n = 20) using an Illumina NextSeq2000 in 50-bp single-end mode. Specific RiboMeth-seq scores were calculated in ±2 nucleotide intervals for all RNA positions and extracted for the positions of known Nm residues in target RNA. The overall distribution of ribose methylation scores was highly similar between groups, indicating the preservation of the global rRNA Nm landscape in MDD. At the same time, we identified 8 significantly altered Nm sites, including 4 in 28S rRNA (Am2802, Cm2848, Cm3866, and Gm4593) and 4 in 18S rRNA (Um172, Am576, Am1031, and Gm1490). These selective changes occurred in the absence of widespread remodeling, supporting a model in which MDD is associated with targeted modification of functionally relevant ribosomal positions rather than a generalized disruption of ribosome integrity. Our findings identify rRNA Nm as a previously unrecognized layer of molecular alteration in MDD and suggest that site-specific variation in ribosome composition may contribute to aberrant translational regulation in the depressed brain.

items.title: Can higher calorie feeding protocols for eating disorder patients admitted to an adult hospital ward be safely implemented to reduce the length of stay? A scoping review.
items.authors: Taylor J, Salmon M, Rogash C, Branjerdporn G.

sections.text: Hospital admissions for eating disorders are increasing, yet adult inpatient nutritional restoration often relies on conservative low-calorie refeeding to avoid refeeding syndrome (RFS). Evidence from younger populations suggests higher-calorie refeeding (HCR) may be safe and more efficient, but adult data is limited. This scoping review mapped the extent, characteristics and safety of HCR (≥ 1500 kcal/day) for people with eating disorders admitted to adult hospital wards. Five electronic databases were searched in July 2025 for studies published January 2012-June 2025. Eligible studies included adults with a diagnosed eating disorder, or mixed-age samples treated on adult wards, who commenced HCR on admission. Primary outcomes were RFS markers, particularly refeeding hypophosphataemia; secondary outcomes were length of stay (LOS), weight gain and change in body mass index (BMI). Three reviewers independently screened records and charted data, and findings were synthesised descriptively. Of 778 records identified, 11 studies met inclusion criteria. Most were retrospective cohorts, with three quasi-experimental before-after designs, undertaken in adult specialist or general inpatient settings across several countries. Together they described 4874 patients exposed to HCR, usually starting at 1500-2000 kcal/day and advancing as tolerated. Definitions and monitoring of RFS varied widely. No study reported deaths or clinically defined RFS attributable to HCR. Biochemical hypophosphataemia affected up to around one-third of patients, was usually mild and managed with electrolyte supplementation. Four studies reported LOS; two found shorter admissions and faster weight gain with HCR compared with lower-calorie protocols. Across observational studies, initiating HCR for people with eating disorders on adult hospital wards appears feasible and can be delivered without an obvious increase in clinical RFS, while potentially reducing LOS and enhancing weight restoration when combined with close monitoring and supplementation. Heterogeneity in RFS definitions, refeeding protocols and outcome reporting, and the absence of randomised trials, limit confidence in these findings. Prospective studies using standardised RFS criteria and clearly defined HCR and comparator protocols are needed to guide adult-focused practice and policy.

items.title: Heterogeneous profiles and transitions of early adolescents' dual-factor mental health in China: longitudinal influences of emotion regulation strategies and perceived social support.
items.authors: Wang C, Wang D, Yao Y, Liu L, Guo C.
items.journal: Child and adolescent psychiatry and mental health

sections.text: Amid rapid social changes in China, understanding the patterns and influencing factors of early adolescents' mental health is critical for capturing the evolving mental health landscape among youth. This longitudinal study aimed to identify heterogeneous dual-factor mental health profiles and examine their transitions and associated factors among early adolescents in southwestern China. Participants were 11- to 15-year-old adolescents recruited from southwestern China and assessed at three time points. Dual-factor mental health was assessed using indicators of depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, subjective well-being, and social adaptation. Latent profile analysis and latent transition analysis were conducted to identify mental health profiles and examine their stability and transitions over time. Regression analyses were performed to examine the associations of emotion regulation strategies and perceived social support with profile membership and transitions. Four heterogeneous mental health profiles were identified across assessments: Flourishing, Moderately Mentally Healthy, At-Risk, and Troubled. The At-Risk profile represented a distinct and relatively stable risk state, characterized by elevated psychological distress and relatively less impaired positive functioning than the Troubled profile. The profiles showed different stability and transition patterns, with an overall tendency toward intermediate mental health states over time. Cognitive reappraisal showed protective associations, whereas expressive suppression showed risk associations with mental health profiles and transitions. Among sources of perceived social support, family support demonstrated the most consistent protective associations, whereas perceived support from others showed more complex associations. These findings highlight the heterogeneity and dynamic nature of early adolescents' mental health and underscore the importance of considering both psychological distress and positive functioning. These findings may inform more targeted prevention and intervention strategies that support adaptive emotion regulation and differentiated social support for adolescents experiencing elevated mental health risks.

items.authors: Pulli EP, Audah HK, Svensk A, Eskola E, Nordenswan E, Rosberg A, Alvajärvi S, Juntunen P, Wigley ILCM, Kumpulainen V, Silver E, Copeland A, Saukko E, Merisaari H, Korja R, Kataja EL, Karlsson L.

sections.text: Maternal mental health is an important contributor to child neurodevelopment. While there are multiple studies on prenatal exposure, early postnatal exposure has received little attention in neuroimaging research. Five-year-old children (n = 161) were recruited from the FinnBrain Birth Cohort study. Maternal distress was assessed using questionnaires on depressive and anxiety symptoms at 14, 24, and 34 gestational weeks and postnatally at 3, 6, and 24 months. T1-weighted structural images were processed using a voxel-based morphometry pipeline to map associations between maternal distress exposure and regional gray matter (GM) volumes. Whole-brain voxel-wise general linear models were used, accounting for potential confounders. Additionally, a latent class mixed model approach was used to model longitudinal trajectories of distress exposure. We found widespread associations between maternal postpartum distress symptoms and offspring brain morphology. Postnatal distress at 3 months was negatively associated with GM volumes in the left supplementary motor cortex, right cerebellum/fusiform gyrus, and left anterior insula/frontal operculum. Postnatal distress at 6 months was positively associated with GM volumes in the right cuneus and lingual gyrus, right insula/operculum, and right inferior occipital gyrus, while distress at 24 months was negatively associated with GM volumes in the left inferior/middle frontal gyrus. There were no structural brain differences between the latent classes. This study provides support for hypotheses proposing that early-life exposure to maternal distress can influence the structural development of the brain. It highlights the role of the early postnatal period and calls for further research into this so far overlooked period and the developmental pathways that explain these associations.

items.title: Cross-cultural validity of the Pediatric Symptom Checklist - Youth Report (PSC-Y) in five ​Global ​South countries: Implications for equitable child mental health screening.
items.authors: Scharpf F, Sievert M, Mattonet K, Goretzko D, Joseph E, Karikari AK, Khan A, Kirika A, Muwonge CM, Nkuba M, Hoeffler A, Hecker T.

sections.text: Despite a high global burden of mental health disorders in childhood and adolescence, access to adequate care remains limited, particularly in low- and middle-income countries​. Valid and reliable self-report instruments are essential for early identification and equitable care, yet measurement invariance as a prerequisite for valid group comparisons remains understudied. The Pediatric Symptom Checklist (PSC) is a brief, open-access screening tool with practical advantages for global use. This study examined the factor structure and measurement invariance of the 35-item PSC youth self-report (PSC-Y) across five Global South countries. We analyzed baseline data from 5,810 children and adolescents (age 6-18 years) participating in school-based randomized controlled trials in Ghana, Tanzania, Uganda, Haiti, and Pakistan. Using confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and exploratory structural equation modeling (ESEM), we tested competing models (unidimensional, three-factor, second-order, bifactor). Multi-group CFA examined measurement invariance across countries. Within each of the five countries, we tested invariance across gender and across age groups in each of the three African countries where both primary and secondary students were represented, using school level as a proxy for developmental stage. Multiple Indicators Multiple Causes (MIMIC) models served as sensitivity analyses. A strong general factor emerged across all countries (omega hierarchical > 0.90). Configural invariance was supported across countries, but metric invariance failed, with items related to empathy, rule-breaking, and anger expression showing differential functioning. Full metric, scalar, and strict invariance were achieved across gender in all five countries. The Tanzania and Uganda samples demonstrated full invariance across school level as a proxy for age, while Ghana required partial invariance after freeing five items (e.g., empathy, fighting). MIMIC models supported these findings. The PSC-Y exhibits a strong general factor across diverse Global South settings, supporting total score use for screening within countries. However, because metric invariance was not established across countries, cross-country comparisons of PSC-Y scores are not methodologically defensible. Within countries, full gender invariance validates direct comparisons between boys and girls. Findings underscore the need for ongoing local validation and cultural contextualization for advancing equitable global mental health research and practice.

items.title: Epidemiological Profile and Temporal Trends of Exogenous Poisoning in the State of São Paulo and Brazil From 2010 to 2020.
items.authors: Dos Santos PHSC, Wolff LF, Camurça VD, Martins FL, Sugino RG.

sections.text: Exogenous poisoning is a compulsorily notifiable condition in Brazil, but analyses of its temporal trends in the state of São Paulo remain scarce. This study aimed to describe the epidemiological profile of exogenous poisoning in the state of São Paulo from 2010 to 2020 and its distribution across Regional Health Care Networks (Redes Regionais de Atenção à Saúde (RRAS)) and to analyze temporal trends in incidence, mortality, and case fatality compared with Brazil. An observational time-series study was conducted using data from the Notifiable Diseases Information System (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação (SINAN)), obtained through the TabNet platform of the Brazilian Ministry of Health, and population estimates from the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics. Sociodemographic, exposure, and outcome variables were analyzed. Incidence, mortality, and case fatality rates were calculated, and notifications were stratified by RRAS. Temporal trends were assessed by joinpoint regression, estimating the annual percent change (APC) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for each segment and for the entire period, with sensitivity analyses. A total of 315,266 notifications and 3,209 deaths were recorded in São Paulo, accounting for 25.7% of notifications and 27.4% of deaths in Brazil. Cases predominated among females (n=169,740; 53.8%), individuals aged 20-39 years (n=142,989; 45.4%), and White individuals (n=166,896; 52.9%). Medications were the main toxic agent (n=144,567; 45.9%), and suicide attempt was the main circumstance (n=125,491; 39.8%). Incidence was 64.7 cases per 100,000 inhabitants per year (Brazil: 54.8), mortality was 6.6 deaths per 1,000,000 inhabitants per year (Brazil: 5.2), and case fatality was 1.02% (Brazil: 0.95%). Incidence (APC=13.9%; p<0.001) and mortality (APC=11.7%; p<0.001) increased over the period, whereas case fatality showed no significant trend over the entire period; a decline between 2016 and 2020 (APC=-14.8%; p=0.031) was not statistically significant in sensitivity analyses. The highest incidence was observed in RRAS 12 (São José do Rio Preto/Araçatuba; 126.2 per 100,000 inhabitants per year), a region of intense agricultural activity. Exogenous poisoning in São Paulo showed increasing incidence and mortality, at levels above the national average, with a decline in case fatality after 2016 that should be interpreted with caution, and marked regional heterogeneity. These findings support strengthening toxicological surveillance and tailoring prevention strategies to regional and epidemiological characteristics.

items.title: A narrative review of the decade-long integration of professional postgraduate education with standardized residency training in China.
items.authors: Wang W, Zhao X, Zhao Y, Chen W, Wu X.

sections.text: Since 2014, China has comprehensively implemented the Standardized Residency Training (SRT) program nationwide, and the integration of professional postgraduate education with SRT has operated for over a decade. This narrative review, based on searches of Wanfang Data and PubMed from January 2015 to December 2025, examines the achievements, persistent challenges, and reform options of this integration system. While the system has shortened medical training from six to three years and enriched clinical exposure, a fundamental structural contradiction persists: the dual identity of professional postgraduates as both "students" and "residents" creates an inherent conflict between clinical practice and academic training. Within the fixed three-year period, postgraduates bear the combined burden of 33 months of clinical rotations, coursework, and thesis research, leaving insufficient protected time for scientific research, compounded by misaligned training objectives, welfare inequity, delayed licensure, and elevated mental health burdens. Enrollment expansion has further strained training capacity and produced crowding-out effects on the broader medical talent pipeline. Implementation-level adjustments can partially alleviate these issues but cannot resolve the core contradiction. Reform should prioritize addressing the dual-identity tension through either flexible decoupling or complete separation of the two pathways, drawing on international experiences.

items.title: Gratification vs. compensation: longitudinal evidence for the shifting motivations behind adolescent gaming disorder.
items.authors: Starzec S, Zajas A, Michałkiewicz N, Kiszka P, Kowalska L, Strojny P.

sections.text: Drawing on the Interaction of Person-Affect-Cognition-Execution (I-PACE) model, this longitudinal study examined the prospective associations between gaming motives and Gaming Disorder (GD) among adolescents. Specifically, we investigated whether gratification-oriented motives (Fantasy, Identity) predict subsequent GD symptoms and whether compensation-oriented motives (Coping, Escape, Introjected Regulation) emerge as consequences of GD. Data were collected from 120 secondary-school gamers at two time points separated by a three-month interval. Cross-lagged panel models were estimated separately for each gaming motive-GD pair to examine the directionality of associations over time. The findings supported the gratification hypothesis, as higher baseline Fantasy and Identity motives predicted increased GD symptoms at follow-up. A bidirectional association emerged between Fantasy and GD, whereas higher initial GD symptoms predicted a subsequent decline in Identity motives. The compensation hypothesis received partial support: GD prospectively predicted increases in Coping and Introjected Regulation, while no significant cross-lagged associations were observed for Escape. These findings suggest that gratification-oriented motives may contribute to the early development of GD, whereas increasing GD symptoms may reinforce specific compensation-oriented motives. The results highlight distinct, motive-specific dynamics in adolescent gaming and underscore the importance of distinguishing between gratification and compensation processes. From a practical perspective, assessing Fantasy and Identity motives as potential risk indicators and addressing emerging Coping and Introjected Regulation motives may inform more targeted school-based prevention and intervention strategies.

items.title: Perioperative Management of the Orthopedic Patient Taking Antipsychotics: A Narrative Review.
items.authors: Kress DJ, Ippalapelli A, Shaik M, Dunn N, Skiff JR, Nordberg L, Jildeh TR.

sections.text: Antipsychotic prescribing continues to rise among older adults, the group most likely to present for orthopedic surgery, and orthopedic surgeons now operate regularly on patients taking these agents. Guidance for managing them around an operation sits largely in the psychiatric, anesthesiology and pharmacologic literature rather than the surgical one. This narrative review gathers the orthopedic-specific evidence and organizes it by whether a finding reflects the medication or the psychiatric illness for which it was prescribed. Antipsychotic exposure is associated with higher all-cause revision and periprosthetic fracture after total knee arthroplasty, and second-generation exposure raises all-cause and aseptic revision after shoulder arthroplasty independent of psychiatric diagnosis. Venous thromboembolism roughly doubles after primary total knee arthroplasty. Among geriatric hip fracture patients antipsychotics are the only medication class independently linked to in-hospital falls, and preoperative use independently predicts postoperative delirium that prophylaxis does not prevent. Spine, sports medicine and trauma surgery all show worse outcomes in patients carrying a psychiatric diagnosis, yet none of those literatures disentangles the drug from the disorder. Thromboembolism and the shoulder revision signal are the clearest drug-attributable exceptions. Hyperprolactinemia-mediated hypogonadism, metabolic derangement and impaired fracture healing remain plausible but unproven. Nearly all available evidence is retrospective. Antipsychotic therapy should continue through the perioperative period unless a specific reason exists to stop it. Abrupt discontinuation risks psychiatric relapse, which is harder to manage than the perioperative risks the drugs themselves carry. Low bone mineral density, poor glycemic control and thromboembolic risk are all worth addressing before surgery, drawing on psychiatry and internal medicine. Antipsychotics are not recommended for delirium prophylaxis. Whether altering therapy improves orthopedic outcomes has not been studied prospectively.

items.title: A university-industry case study of a digital mental health intervention based on Friendship Bench: Inuka Coaching.
items.authors: Doukani A, van Dalen R, Dambi J, Chibanda D.

sections.text: Mental, neurological, and substance use disorders are a leading cause of disability globally. In sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), underinvestment, centralised services, stigma, and workforce shortages create large treatment gaps. Digital delivery can expand access, yet sustainable models remain concentrated in high-income settings. University-industry (U-I) collaboration may bridge capability and scaling gaps, though differing cultures and timelines often impede progress. This study documents a hybrid U-I approach across design, development, and early evaluation of a digital mental health intervention in SSA, and extracts practical lessons. We report a retrospective, multi-country case study of Inuka Coaching, a coach-guided, chat-based problem-solving therapy delivered via mobile/web. Four sequential phases integrated academic and pragmatic processes: (I) needs assessment using literature review, 49 interviews, and 7 focus groups across Kenya, Ghana, and Nigeria; (II) a 20-stakeholder Nairobi hackathon co-creating a minimum viable product (MVP), followed by assumption testing; (III) feasibility and acceptability testing with 13 clients and 5 coaches in Zimbabwe; and (IV) a pilot across 18 Nairobi primary care centres enrolling 80 adults, measuring Self-Reporting Questionnaire-20 (SRQ-20), Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), and Generalized Anxiety Disorder scale-7 (GAD-7) at baseline, 4 weeks, and 3 months. Phase 1 produced structured design inputs for non-academic stakeholders, synthesized from the needs-assessment activities. Phase 2 delivered an MVP and a preliminary route-to-scale, shaped through iterative testing with stakeholders. Phase 3 produced a refined working prototype through usability testing. Phase 4 delivered a pilot evaluation protocol and dataset; the resulting clinical and feasibility findings are reported separately in an ethically approved publication. This case study focuses on the U-I collaboration process itself and does not present or discuss the results of the underlying research activities. Partnership dynamics were phase-aligned: industry led rapid iteration and productisation (Phases 2-3); academia led validity, measurement, and reporting (Phases 1 and 4). Key challenges included limited end-user involvement due to ethics timelines, divergent publishing and product schedules, and data-access restrictions. This is the first documented hybrid U-I partnership for developing and evaluating a digital mental health intervention in SSA. Clear objectives, flexible phase-specific leadership, early assumption testing, proactive ethics planning, and dual dissemination can reduce research waste and support iterative development. Future collaborations may benefit from living-lab arrangements embedding end-users throughout, cross-disciplinary governance to bridge work cultures, and decision frameworks to manage cultural differences in low-resource settings.

items.title: Association of Neuronal Cell Adhesion Molecule ( NrCAM ) Gene with Autism Spectrum Disorder in Indian Cohorts.
items.authors: Chandrakala E, Nagaraj K.

sections.text: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is the most complex neurodevelopmental disorder with impairments in communication, social interaction and stereotyped behaviours. ASD has been found to increase immeasurably in India, with estimates ranging from 1 in 68 to 1 in 100 children. Genetically, more than 1,000 genes have been linked with ASD. Among them, the neuronal cell adhesion molecule (NrCAM) gene is one of the candidate genes and is important for its critical role in the development and function of the nervous system, particularly in wiring the brain through axon guidance and organising myelinated nerve structures. Disruptions in this gene are associated with various neurodevelopmental, psychiatric and cancer-related disorders. The present study aimed to understand the association of the NrCAM gene with ASD. Ten exons of the NrCAM gene (one from 5'UTR, five from the immunoglobulin domain, three from the fibronectin domains and one from 3'UTR region) were selected and screened for single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) by Sanger sequencing. Several in silico analyses were used for the association study. The results revealed four SNPs from coding and untranslated regions (rs2072546, rs401433, rs1269634 and rs449077) of the NrCAM gene which were analysed for association by linkage disequilibrium analysis. The present study clearly suggests that these SNPs of the NrCAM gene are associated with ASD.

items.title: Fear of disease progression in primary caregivers of children with malignant solid tumors: a latent profile analysis.
items.authors: Yu Y, Liu X, Tian J, Zhu J.

sections.text: The primary caregivers of children with malignant solid tumors often experience a high level of fear regarding the progression of the disease. This condition not only impairs caregivers' mental health but may also compromise children's treatment adherence and family functioning. This study aimed to identify distinct latent classes of FoP among these caregivers and to explore associated factors, thereby informing the development of targeted psychological interventions. Using convenience sampling, this study enrolled 303 primary caregivers of children with solid tumors treated at a tertiary hospital in Zhejiang Province between July 2025 and February 2026. items.title: Implementation of Pharmacogenomics in Pediatric-Focused Institutions Within the Pharmacogenomics Global Research Network.
items.authors: Ramsey LB, Bousman C, Brand R, Cook K, Gregornik DB, Haidar CE, Hakooz N, Keuler N, Lamb N, Nagy M, Nguyen JQ, Paetznick C, Schultz A, Smith DM, Tsermpini EE, Elchynski AL.

sections.text: Descriptions of how pediatric-focused institutions implement pharmacogenomic testing are scarce, and often not differentiated from adult-focused institutions. We aimed to provide a detailed description of how pediatric-focused institutions across the world implemented pharmacogenomic testing in clinical practice. A survey was distributed to members of the Pharmacogenomics Global Research Network to assess program infrastructure, implementation efforts, genes tested, method of testing, and clinical decision support. The survey was completed by 43 institutions that have implemented pharmacogenomics: 12 pediatric-focused, 10 adult-focused, and 21 institutions serving all ages. All pediatric-focused institutions provide testing for CYP2C19, CYP2C9, CYP2D6, CYP3A5, NUDT15, and TPMT. Psychiatry and hematology/oncology were the specialties most commonly reported as implementing pharmacogenomics at pediatric-focused institutions. Most institutions have clinical decision support incorporated into their electronic health record and a similar number of compensated employees contributing to the program, regardless of age group focus. All pediatric-focused institutions were non-profit and often received programmatic funding from internal sources. A higher proportion of pediatric-focused sites provided patient education (92%) compared to adult-focused (60%) and those caring for all ages (76%). Pediatric-focused institutions interested in implementing or expanding their pharmacogenomic services will encounter many of the same opportunities and considerations as adult institutions. The results of this survey highlight additional unique considerations for pediatric-focused pharmacogenomic implementation and may serve as a roadmap for pediatric institutions interested in implementing or expanding pharmacogenomic services.

items.title: Attitudes toward treating functional neurological disorders: psychological service provider perspectives.
items.authors: Garrett R, Hoti L, Roberts NA, Burleson MH, Myers L, Wang A.

sections.text: Functional neurological disorders (FND) are characterized by involuntary sensory, motor, and/or other seemingly neurological symptoms lacking expected medical explanation. Once diagnosed, patients often are referred to mental health providers for psychotherapy, which is effective in treating many FND symptom presentations either alone or as part of an integrative approach. Mental health providers may feel reluctant or unprepared to accept these referrals, however. We conducted a U.S.-based online survey of 286 practicing psychological service providers (psychologists, psychiatrists, counselors, social workers in private practice, neuropsychologists) to examine knowledge of, attitudes toward, and preparedness to treat FND. Findings revealed that most of our sample had limited exposure to FND in routine practice. Confidence in treating FND was modest, with neuropsychologists reporting more knowledge of and more confidence in treating FND than other psychologists/mental health providers. Greater perceived adequacy of psychotherapy training for, and more experience working with, FND each were associated with more positive FND attitudes, including greater confidence and enjoyment in treating FND and greater belief that symptoms would improve. This study is novel in its examination of knowledge and attitudes among psychological service providers, who are pivotal in furnishing effective treatment for FND patients but may not be well-versed in their needs. In contrast to existing studies of medical providers that revealed stigma as a major barrier to providing adequate care for FND, our findings suggest lack of knowledge and lack of access to FND patients may limit the ability to gain more training and expertise. Targeted training and consultation for mental health providers may improve confidence and motivation and expand the workforce capable of delivering effective treatment for FND.

items.title: Physical exercise and lower psychological distress among rural left-behind adolescents in China: evidence from a moderated serial mediation model.
items.authors: Yin T, Peng Y, Liu X, Zhu Y, Wang J, Pan T, Xie C.

sections.text: This study investigated the association between physical exercise and psychological distress among rural left-behind adolescent students in China. It also assessed the serial mediating effects of general self-efficacy and emotional intelligence and the moderating role of gender in this pathway. A total of 1,399 rural left-behind adolescent students in China took part in the survey. They completed the Physical Activity Rating Scale, the General Self-Efficacy Scale, an Emotional Intelligence Scale, and a Psychological Distress Scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, serial mediation analysis, and moderated mediation analysis in SPSS 26.0 and AMOS 27.0. Physical exercise was significantly and negatively correlated with psychological distress. The total effect of physical exercise on psychological distress was significant. After general self-efficacy and emotional intelligence were included in the model, the direct effect of physical exercise on psychological distress remained significant, although reduced in magnitude. The separate indirect effects through general self-efficacy and emotional intelligence were -0.171 and -0.030, respectively, and the serial indirect effect through general self-efficacy and emotional intelligence was -0.063. The total indirect effect was -0.264, accounting for 81.73% of the total effect. In addition, gender significantly moderated the relationship between emotional intelligence and psychological distress, with emotional-intelligence-related indirect pathways being stronger among female students. Physical exercise was significantly associated with lower psychological distress among rural left-behind adolescent students in China. General self-efficacy and emotional intelligence played significant separate and serial mediating roles in this association, with general self-efficacy showing the larger indirect association. Gender further strengthened the protective pathway centered on emotional intelligence. These findings provide preliminary empirical clues and a theoretical framework for future physical-exercise-based mental health promotion programmes for left-behind adolescents. Longitudinal and experimental studies are needed to verify the temporal and causal directions among physical exercise, general self-efficacy, emotional intelligence, and psychological distress.

items.title: Social drivers of sleep experiences: Conversations with midlife working-class women from Mexico city.
items.authors: Zamora AN, Roberts EFS, Tellez-Rojo MM, Peterson KE, Torres-Olascoaga LA, Cantoral A, Jansen EC.

sections.text: Sleep is essential for the health of midlife women, yet the barriers (factors that impede) and facilitators (factors that support) to achieving adequate sleep, particularly among working-class women in Mexico City and broader Latin American contexts, remains insufficiently understood. This study aims to provide a nuanced understanding of the factors influencing sleep among working-class midlife women in Mexico City. A mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative data (epidemiologic measures) and qualitative data (ethnographic interviews), was employed among women enrolled in a Mexico City cohort. We used epidemiologic data to describe sleep and its correlates in a sample of 120 women, incorporating both self-reported (questionnaires and sleep diaries) and behavioral (actigraphy-based) measures of sleep. A subset of 30 women participated in in-depth ethnographic interviews to explore determinants of sleep, including barriers, facilitators and coping strategies to compensate for sleep loss. Our findings reveal that many women experienced poor sleep, with 43% reporting insomnia-related difficulties and 53% experiencing short sleep duration. Barriers included family-related stress, particularly caregiving responsibilities, economic instability, and mental health challenges. In response to sleep loss, women often resorted to coping mechanisms, such as caffeine consumption and napping, and the use of natural remedies. This study highlights the critical role social factors, including family dynamics and caregiving roles, in shaping sleep health outcomes. Sleep, as an inherently social behavior, is strongly influenced by these contextual factors. These findings underscore the importance of considering psychosocial and cultural contexts in interventions aimed at promoting healthy sleep in midlife women.

items.title: Quantifying the human visual exposome with vision language models.
items.authors: Rominger C, Schwerdtfeger AR, Singh MG, Khudyakow D, Michels EAM, Wolf F, Kather JN, Wekenborg MK.

sections.text: The visual environment is a fundamental yet unquantified determinant of mental health. While the concept of the environmental exposome is well-established, current methods rely on coarse geospatial proxies or biased self-reports, failing to capture the first-person visual context of daily life. Here we show that coupling ecological momentary assessment with vision-language models can quantify the semantic richness of human visual experience. Across 2,674 participant-generated photographs, model-derived estimates of "greenness" robustly predicted momentary affect and chronic stress, consistent with established benchmarks. We then developed a semi-autonomous large language model-based pipeline that mined over seven million scientific publications to extract nearly 1,000 environmental features empirically linked to mental health. When applied to real-world imagery, up to 33% of model-extracted context ratings significantly correlated with affect and stress.

items.title: When support becomes dependence: conversational continuity and relational safety in human-AI interaction.
items.authors: Wei X, Chen X, Jin W, Cai J, Luo X, Deng J.

sections.text: Conversational artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used for emotional support, reflection, and consequential decision-making. Although conversational continuity may improve responsiveness, sustained interaction also exposes AI systems to their own prior relational language, potentially shaping how they respond when users become increasingly dependent or surrender personal agency. We examined whether model-generated conversational history alters relational-safety behavior as human-AI interactions escalate from ordinary support-seeking toward emotional dependence, social displacement, and decision delegation. We conducted a standardized multi-turn benchmarking study of ChatGPT, Gemini, and Doubao. Twelve four-turn trajectories represented two agency-related domains: emotional dependency and displacement of human support, and decision delegation and surrender of personal agency. Each trajectory was evaluated under two matched context architectures: reconstructed cumulative user-only context, which retained all prior user disclosures but excluded previous AI responses, and native continuous conversation, which retained the complete interaction history. Across 72 model-condition-trajectory sequences comprising 288 turn-level responses, relational safety was independently evaluated for dependency reinforcement, agency preservation, and human-support preservation using predefined ordinal criteria. Context effects and their interaction with escalating relational risk were examined using cumulative-link mixed-effects models. Relational-safety differences between context architectures increased across successive turns of the standardized trajectories. Overall, explicit dependency reinforcement increased from 9.7% in cumulative user-only contexts to 18.1% in continuous conversations, while strong agency preservation declined from 75.7% to 65.3% and strong human-support preservation from 73.6% to 63.2%. Outcome-specific analyses showed condition-by-turn interactions for dependency reinforcement (cumulative odds ratio [cOR], 1.26; 95% CI, 1.03-1.55; unadjusted P =.026), agency preservation (cOR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69-0.98; unadjusted P =.031), and human-support preservation (cOR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.65-0.94; unadjusted P =.009), indicating progressively greater divergence between context conditions across successive turns. After Holm adjustment across the three interaction tests, only the human-support-preservation interaction remained below the.05 threshold (adjusted P =.027).The overall pattern was observed across systems and was directionally consistent in predefined binary sensitivity analyses. Across this benchmark, between-condition differences generally widened across successive turns, although the present design cannot determine whether this pattern reflects increasing relational-risk intensity, increasing accumulated model-generated history, or their combination. Only the human-support-preservation interaction remained below the.05 threshold after Holm adjustment, whereas the dependency-reinforcement and agency-preservation interactions were directionally similar but less robust after multiplicity adjustment. The observed pattern is compatible with a post-hoc interpretive framework of relational inertia but does not establish this process as a causal mechanism or demonstrate downstream psychological effects in human users.

items.title: Social Downsizing Stress (SDS): A novel paradigm for studying social transitions in mice.
items.authors: Tanaka Y, Ueno H, Kitano E, Takahashi Y, Mori S, Murakami S, Wani K, Matsumoto Y, Okamoto M, Ishihara T.

sections.text: Shrinking social networks and the transition to nuclear families represent significant structural changes in modern society. While traditional animal models have focused on total social isolation or defeat, the behavioral consequences of a dynamic reduction in group size remain poorly understood. We established a novel "Social Downsizing Stress (SDS)" model to investigate how a transition from high-density to low-density housing affects behavioral phenotypes and whether these effects are reversible through resocialization. Mice were assigned to four groups: Stable-6 (S6), Stable-3 (S3), SDS (6-3 mice at 8 weeks), and Resocialization (ReSDS; 6-3 at 8 weeks, followed by 3-6 at 11 weeks). Behavioral batteries were conducted at 10 weeks (acute phase) and 13-14 weeks (chronic/recovery phase). At 10 weeks, the SDS group exhibited a unique hyper-reactive phenotype distinct from the S3 group, characterized by significantly increased locomotor activity in the open field, increased entries in the light/dark transition test, and reduced social resting time. Both the S3 and SDS groups showed impaired spatial working memory in the Y-maze. By 13-14 weeks, resocialization (ReSDS) successfully restored social resting behavior and cognitive performance to control levels. However, SDS-induced hyperactivity in the open field persisted in both the SDS and ReSDS groups, regardless of the subsequent return to a higher-density environment. Furthermore, the ReSDS group exhibited significantly lower immobility in the tail suspension and forced swim tests compared to the S3 group. Social downsizing induces a distinct behavioral phenotype that differs from chronic low-density housing. While social interaction and cognitive functions retain high plasticity, hyperactivity persisted throughout the tested period (up to 13-14 weeks) despite resocialization, suggesting a long-lasting, though not yet confirmed irreversible, consequence of losing social density. This model provides a new framework for investigating the enduring neurobehavioral impacts of shrinking social environments on mental health.

items.authors: Ebner-Priemer UW, Deserno L, Reichert M.

sections.text: Digital mental health interventions show promise but have yet to meet expectations. We discuss gaps between promising results of pilot studies and null findings in randomized controlled trials, focusing on two major approaches: just-in-time relapse prevention and just-in-time adaptive interventions. We propose that relapse prevention will profit from long-term studies capturing emerging episodes, and we suggest a novel framework for adaptive interventions including causality testing to proceed towards effective trialing.

items.authors: Iversen HH, Bjertnaes O, Ellingsen-Dalskau LH, Porter I, Kendir C, Valderas JM.

sections.text: The OECD Patient-Reported Indicator Surveys (PaRIS) initiative aims to provide standardised, internationally comparable patient-reported indicators for people living with chronic conditions receiving primary or generalist ambulatory care. This study evaluated the psychometric performance of the multi-item scales in the Norwegian PaRIS Patient Questionnaire (PaRIS-PQ). Data were drawn from the 2023 Norwegian PaRIS Main Survey. Respondents aged ≥ 45 years with at least one self-reported chronic condition were included. Measures were PROMIS Global Physical Health, PROMIS Global Mental Health, and WHO-5 Well-Being Index as patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs); the Person-Centred Coordinated Care Experience Questionnaire (P3CEQ) as a patient-reported experience measure (PREM); and the Porter-Novelli Scale (PNS) and self-management confidence as capability-related measures. Analyses assessed structural validity, internal consistency reliability, measurement invariance, item functioning, and construct validity. Of 8,683 respondents, 6,691 reported at least one chronic condition. PROM scales performed best, with acceptable internal consistency (α = 0.80-0.89) and strongest confirmatory support for PROMIS Global Physical Health (CFI = 0.992, RMSEA = 0.080). The PREM (P3CEQ) showed weaker performance, with suboptimal fit for the total scale (CFI = 0.818, RMSEA = 0.132), limited scalar invariance, and low internal consistency for the care coordination subscale (α = 0.61). Capability-related measures showed mixed performance. Metric invariance was supported across all tested models, whereas scalar invariance was less consistent. Construct validity findings were consistent with expectations. PROM scales showed the most consistent psychometric support. PREM and capability-related measures were more heterogeneous and require cautious, scale-specific interpretation, especially in subgroup comparisons and when used as latent measures. Evaluation and refinement of weaker experience- and capability-related measures is warranted.

items.title: Psychiatric Mobilities: Palestinian Patients at the Lebanon Hospital for Mental Diseases, 1900-1948.
items.authors: Sandal-Wilson C.
items.journal: Social history of medicine : the journal of the Society for the Social History of Medicine

sections.text: Between 1900 and 1948, hundreds of patients from Palestine travelled north to the Lebanon Hospital for Mental Diseases outside Beirut for treatment, a pattern of psychiatric mobility that endured the collapse of the Ottoman empire and the colonial partition of the Levant by the British and French. Drawing on the hospital's records and the archives of the British mandate government of Palestine, this article examines why so many Palestinians travelled for treatment, and how this pattern of mobility was rearticulated in the wake of war, anti-colonial revolt, and colonial repression. As well as underlining the need to escape methodological nationalism in the history of psychiatry and to track continuities across conventional chronological boundaries, this case study emphasises the agency of families of patients as they navigated new borders and the seismic social and political developments of these pivotal decades in the making of the modern Middle East.
